name: Hulhumale
tagline: Reclaimed island with space and newer flats
description: A planned island north of the airport, laid out on a grid of wide roads, low-rise apartment blocks and a long artificial beach. Phase 1 has cafes, supermarkets and small offices, Phase 2 is dense new housing towers. Remote workers pick it for quiet, modern flats with real windows and lifts.
bestFor: Nomads who want a calm, newly built apartment and can live away from the old-city bustle.
pros: Newer buildings with lifts and reliable water
Beach and open promenade on the doorstep
Direct bridge and bus link to the airport
cons: Feels sterile and half-built in places
Bus or taxi needed for anything in Male proper
Very little shade, brutal midday heat

name: Henveiru
tagline: Eastern Male with embassies and the seafront
description: The eastern quarter of Male island, holding ministries, embassies, the artificial beach and most of the better cafes. Streets are narrow, scooter-packed and lined with tall thin buildings, but almost everything a resident needs sits within a ten minute walk. The most sought-after address on the island.
bestFor: Nomads who want the best cafes, coworking and ferry links within walking distance.
pros: Walk to cafes, banks and the artificial beach
Closest to the Hulhumale and Villingili ferry terminals
Best internet and backup power on the island
cons: Constant scooter noise and no green space
Apartments are small with poor natural light

name: Maafannu
description: Male's largest and most crowded district, covering the western half of the island around the commercial harbour and the fish market. Streets are packed with hardware shops, guesthouses, cheap Sri Lankan and Bangladeshi eateries and low-cost flats. This is where most working residents actually live rather than visit.
bestFor: Budget nomads willing to trade comfort for the cheapest central rooms in Male.
pros: Cheapest rooms and studios on Male island
Everything reachable on foot in minutes
cons: Extremely dense, loud and short on daylight
Harbour traffic and delivery trucks all day
Older buildings with weaker water pressure

name: Galolhu
description: The central and southern strip of Male, wedged between the busier districts and fronting the southern harbour. It is mostly residential blocks, small mosques, the national stadium and neighbourhood grocers, with fewer tourists than Henveiru. Rents sit below the eastern seafront while keeping the same short walking distances.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads who want a normal local street rather than a cafe strip.
pros: Cheaper than Henveiru for similar flats
Central enough to walk anywhere on the island
cons: Almost no cafes suitable for working
Traffic funnels through on the main roads
Very little open or green space

name: Villimale
tagline: Car-free island a short ferry away
description: The fifth district of Male City, an island two kilometres west reached by a 24 hour ferry that takes about ten minutes. Cars are effectively banned, so it is bicycles, sandy lanes, mature trees and a swimmable beach on the western side. Quiet, green and the closest thing to island life within the capital.
bestFor: Nomads prioritising calm, trees and a swim over being in the thick of the capital.
pros: No cars, so genuinely quiet streets
cons: Every trip depends on the ferry timetable
Thin choice of shops, cafes and clinics
